scope: Evidence that can validate fisheries production physics, pre-1337 access technology, and uncertainty. No record in this registry is a population-capacity training target.
forbidden_uses: EU5 starting population or RGO fields
modern reported catch as a location label
archaeological population estimates as fisheries-production truth when catch was derived from those same population estimates

sources.title: ESGF CMIP6 PMIP past1000 intpp catalogue query
page_table_figure_refs: facet_counts.facet_fields.source_id: MIROC-ES2L only; query run 2026-08-03
supports: The public CMIP6 PMIP past1000 catalogue does not currently supply a three-model ocean intpp ensemble.
limitations: Catalogue availability can change and must be re-queried before acquisition.

sources.title: PMIP4 experiments using MIROC-ES2L Earth system model
page_table_figure_refs: Sections 2 and 3; PMIP4 experiment and Earth-system-model description
supports: MIROC-ES2L is a coupled Earth-system simulation suitable as one physical medieval-ocean trajectory.
limitations: One model cannot measure structural disagreement among ocean-biogeochemistry models.

sources.title: A new global oceanic multi-model net primary productivity data product
page_table_figure_refs: Section 2 and Figures 3-7; five satellite NPP algorithms and ensemble variance
supports: Algorithm choice creates material spatial and temporal NPP disagreement and should be propagated.
limitations: The product is satellite-era and cannot by itself supply a circa-1337 climate anomaly.

sources.title: Primary production required to sustain global fisheries
page_table_figure_refs: Pages 255-257; abstract and 48-model trophic-transfer calculation
supports: Mean trophic transfer efficiency near 10 percent was re-estimated across 48 published trophic models.
limitations: Reported modern catches enter the paper's primary-production-required calculation and therefore cannot be used as historical labels here.

sources.title: Fish production in freshwaters: Are rivers more productive than lakes?
page_table_figure_refs: Pages 631-643; abstract and river/lake community-production synthesis
supports: The study reports 55 river and 22 lake sites and large between-system differences in community production.
limitations: Cross-site means are not location-specific medieval distributions.

sources.title: Predicting riverine fish production using empirical models and the metabolic theory of ecology
page_table_figure_refs: Abstract; Sections 2-4; independent 78-site validation and reported RMSE
supports: Environment- and assemblage-conditioned transfer models can be validated against held-out fish-production observations.
limitations: Most sites are North American; the authors characterize estimates as rough and call for tests in new regions.

sources.title: Interpreting the expansion of sea fishing in medieval Europe using stable isotope analysis of archaeological cod bones
page_table_figure_refs: Figures 1-4 and Appendix 1; 300 archaeological cod bones
supports: Medieval fishing and preserved-fish trade reached beyond immediate urban waters.
limitations: Distant traded fish cannot validate intrinsic food capacity of the importing location.

sources.title: Stable isotope evidence for late medieval origins of the eastern Baltic cod fishery
page_table_figure_refs: Figures 1-4 and supporting archaeological specimen table
supports: A spatially distinct eastern Baltic cod fishery is directly evidenced in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries.
limitations: Bone provenance identifies exploitation geography, not annual sustainable yield.

sources.title: Midden volume, harvested fish biomass, and pre-contact minimum population estimates for Nuu-chah-nulth Territories in Barkley Sound
page_table_figure_refs: Abstract and dissertation biomass-model chapters; 241,253 cubic metres of midden and approximately 1.2 billion fish over three millennia
supports: A conservative archaeological workflow links midden volume to harvested biomass and food-energy support.
limitations: The estimate averages three millennia and is validation-only, not a 1337 training target.

sources.title: Pre-Columbian fisheries catch reconstruction for a subtropical estuary in South America
page_table_figure_refs: Methods and Results catch-reconstruction tables; accepted manuscript repository record
supports: Archaeological assemblages can provide a long-run check on plausible fish extraction.
limitations: The 73,117.49-tonne estimate is averaged over roughly 5,850 years and is therefore retained only as a conservative held-out lower bound, never a 1337 annual target.

sources.title: Freshwater aquaculture development in China
page_table_figure_refs: Section 2.6 and Table 10; Song Dynasty fry capture, transport and sales
supports: Freshwater aquaculture and organized fry transport were historically available before 1337 in China.
limitations: Modern production tables on the same page cannot be used as medieval output rates.

sources.title: Huilua Fishpond
page_table_figure_refs: Construction-date and fishpond-engineering sections; many Hawaiian ponds dated 1200-1600
supports: Brackish fishpond engineering was feasible within the target historical window in Hawaii.
limitations: The page does not provide a defensible annual yield distribution.

sources.title: Climatic and morphoedaphic indices of fish yields from natural lakes
page_table_figure_refs: Abstract and 43-natural-lake regression tables; mean annual temperature explains 74 percent of yield variance
supports: Lake yield varies systematically with climate and morphoedaphic conditions; a single cross-site mean is not a location label.
limitations: The regression sample is modern and geographically incomplete; it is used only to validate the width of the physical envelope.

sources.title: Review of tropical reservoirs and their fisheries
page_table_figure_refs: Yield-model and comparative lake/reservoir tables in the FAO Fisheries Technical Paper synthesis
supports: Tropical lake and reservoir production supplies a geographic family independent of temperate North American studies.
limitations: Modern managed reservoirs are not medieval labels and remain transfer-validation evidence only.

sources.title: Historical review of Hawaiian coastal fishponds
page_table_figure_refs: Historical section: first pond before 1300; 340-360 ponds, 2,655 ha, estimated 396 kg/ha/year and about 1,050 tonnes/year
supports: Brackish fishpond technology existed by the target period and supplies a held-out one-sided production check.
limitations: The archipelago aggregate is mapped to the Hawaiian EU5 island set and is never assigned to one port or used for training.

sources.title: The English herring fishery in the fourteenth century
page_table_figure_refs: Great Yarmouth landing series: more than 5,000 tonnes in 1336-37 and more than 2,000 tonnes in seven years, 1331-1368
supports: Contemporary accounts provide an in-period minimum extraction check for the southern North Sea fishery.
limitations: Landings include nonlocal vessels and validate a broad fishery ground, not urban intrinsic capacity.

sources.title: Scarborough medieval fisheries documentary evidence
page_table_figure_refs: 1304-05 customs account: 355 lasts, approximately 810 tonnes or 3.55 million herring
supports: An in-period customs account supplies a one-sided fishery lower bound.
limitations: Foreign landings and uncertain grounds preclude use as a local capacity target.

sources.title: A brief history of aquatic resource use in medieval Europe
page_table_figure_refs: North Norwegian stockfish export discussion: approximately 2,000-4,000 tonnes annually around 1300
supports: Exports provide a conservative lower bound on northern Norwegian production in the target period.
limitations: Catch grounds span a broad coast and the export series omits local consumption.

sources.title: Assessment of fishing effort in Parakrama Samudra, an ancient man-made lake in Sri Lanka
page_table_figure_refs: Study-site history and annual-yield estimate near 120 kg/ha/year
supports: A pre-1337 reservoir footprint has a separately measured out-of-period production analogue.
limitations: Modern ecological production is validation-only; it does not establish a medieval harvest rate.

sources.title: The Continuum of Long-Term Lake Fisheries Management
page_table_figure_refs: Medieval Lake Constance fishery and regulation chronology, thirteenth-fifteenth centuries
supports: Lake Constance had a persistent managed freshwater fishery in the target period.
limitations: No independent annual catch interval is promoted; the case tests positive capacity only.

required_artifacts.reason: The current 90 scenarios share one MIROC-ES2L medieval anomaly; three satellite algorithms do not replace medieval climate-model structural uncertainty.
Independent p10/p50/p90 knob combinations are sensitivity bounds, not probabilistic uncertainty.
Cross-site river and lake means must be transferred with same-geography physical predictors and grouped validation.
Human access and sustainable extraction require held-out quantitative preindustrial checks, not only archaeological presence.
The current labels omit geographically restricted pre-1337 aquaculture such as Song Chinese pond culture and Hawaiian fishpond engineering.
